sections.label: Copyright balance rights owners users
sections.summary: Copyright law balances rights owners' limited rights to restrict use with limitations and exceptions allowing public use without encumbrance.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To do so, copyright law needs to strike a fair balance between, on the one hand, "rights owners", who are the owners of copyright or rights of protected performances and users on the other hand.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This balance is achieved by giving rights owners the right, for a limited duration, to prevent or restrict others from using their works or protected performances while also providing limitations and exceptions to those rights to allow the public to use those works or protected performances without encumbrance.

sections.label: Comprehensive review of Copyright Act
sections.summary: A comprehensive review of the Copyright Act included public consultations in 2016, 2017 and 2020 to keep the balance fair.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: All of these changes impact the creation and the use of copyright.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We embarked on a comprehensive review of the Copyright Act to ensure that the balance between rights owners and users continues to be a fair and balanced one even with these changes afoot.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The review included a series of public consultations in 2016, 2017 and most recently, in 2020.

sections.label: Bill repeals re-enacts Copyright Act
sections.summary: The Bill, if passed, will repeal and re-enact the existing Copyright Act.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Bill, if passed, will repeal and re-enact the existing Copyright Act.

sections.label: New right authors performers identified
sections.summary: Divisions 1 and 2 of Part 7 create a new right for authors and performers to be identified for due recognition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Divisions 1 and 2 of Part 7 of the Bill create a new right for authors and performers to be identified in order to accord them due recognition for their creative works.

sections.label: Creators default copyright owners
sections.summary: Clause 133 provides that creators will generally be the default copyright owners, subject to contract.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Another change, Sir, can be found in clause 133 of the Bill, which provides that creators will generally be the default copyright owners, subject to contract.

sections.label: Liability for unauthorised content dealers
sections.summary: Clauses 150 and 445(b) impose civil and criminal liability on commercial dealers in devices, applications and services facilitating access to unauthorised content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Next, for copyright owners of audio-visual content like films and cable programmes, clauses 150 and 445(b) of the Bill impose civil and criminal liability on commercial dealers in hardware devices, software applications and services that facilitate access to unauthorised content.

sections.label: No liability for consumers
sections.summary: The new provisions do not impose liability on consumers and users of hardware devices, software applications or services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The new provisions do not impose liability on consumers and users of the hardware devices, software applications or services.

sections.label: Internet materials for education
sections.summary: Clause 204 creates a new permitted use of Internet materials for educational activities, including home-based teaching and learning by non-profit educational institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Clause 204 of the Bill creates a new permitted use of Internet materials for educational activities, including home-based teaching and learning conducted by non-profit educational institutions.

sections.label: Print disability fee removal
sections.summary: Division 4 of Part 5 modifies permitted uses for persons with print disabilities to remove the obligation to pay fees to the rights owner for conversions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Consequently, Division 4 of Part 5 of the Bill, modifies the permitted uses relating to persons with print disabilities to remove the obligation to pay fees to the rights owner when conversions are made and distributed.

sections.label: Computational data analysis use
sections.summary: Clause 244 allows the use of works and recordings of protected performances for computational data analysis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Another change, Sir, is found in clause 244 of the Bill, which allows the use of works and recordings of protected performances for computational data analysis.

sections.label: Class licensing for CMOs
sections.summary: Divisions 1 and 2 of Part 9 create a new class licensing scheme setting minimum standards for how Collective Management Organisations operate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Divisions 1 and 2 of Part 9 create a new class licensing scheme that sets minimum standards for how Collective Management Organisations, or CMOs, operate.

sections.label: CMO framework by IPOS
sections.summary: The new CMO regulatory framework will be administered by the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore and will address transparency, governance, accountability and efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In this Bill, the new CMO regulatory framework will be administered by the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS) and will address issues of transparency, governance, accountability and efficiency.

sections.label: IPOS licence enforcement powers
sections.summary: IPOS will have powers to set licence conditions, investigate contraventions and impose penalties for non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: IPOS, however, will be vested with powers to set licence conditions, investigate contraventions of licence conditions and also impose penalties for non-compliance.

sections.label: Offence categories and penalties
sections.summary: Offences are categorised into those with a commercial element carrying a higher penalty and those without, carrying lower penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Offences are now categorised into those with commercial element, which share the same higher penalty and those without a commercial element, which attracts a lower range of penalties.

sections.label: CMO licensing implementation timing
sections.summary: The CMO licensing provisions in Division 2 of Part 9 and clause 507(4)(c) will be implemented later after consultation next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The provisions on the licensing of CMOs, which Members will find in Division 2 of Part 9 and clause 507(4)(c) will be implemented later, after we further consult next year on the licence conditions for CMOs, which will be embodied in the subsidiary legislation.

sections.label: Default first ownership of works
sections.summary: Creators of works such as photographs, portraits, engravings, sound recordings and films are by default first owner unless a written agreement states otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The clause provides that creators of certain type of works like photographs, portraits, engravings, sound recordings and films will by default be the first owner of the works, unless there is a contrary intention in a written agreement.

sections.label: Standard template agreement request
sections.summary: The question asks whether a standard template agreement could be provided on the IPOS or CASE website for consumers to retain copyright.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry also consider providing a standard template for a written agreement in the IPOS or in the Consumers' Association (CASE) website, so that consumers can easily reply on the template agreement to retain the copyright to their videos or photographs.

sections.label: Education costs and copyright exemptions
sections.summary: The passage asks about education cost impacts, extending clause 204's exception to all educational institutions, IPC exemptions, and clause 150 infringement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Has the Government assessed the financial impact of the increased costs of education to these students?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In the larger picture, would it not be better for the Government to encourage education by making it less costly?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I wish to ask the Government to consider extending the exception under clause 204 to all educational institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify whether Institutions of a Public Character (IPCs), which have been set up as non-profit entities and exist for charitable purposes can be granted the same exemption under clause 204?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Clause 150 makes it an infringement of copyright if a person makes a device or provides a service and so on to access works communicated without authority.

sections.label: Regulating CMOs collecting royalties
sections.summary: The speaker says consumers have limited negotiating power with CMOs and asks what recourse exists if CMO fees are unreasonable or exorbitant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: As a consumer, he has limited negotiating powers to deal with such CMOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Hence, I think it is helpful to regulate such organisations that collect royalties or fees so that there is greater transparency as to the ownership of the copyright and the fees payable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: What is the recourse of the individual or business or any entity if the fees charged by the CMOs are unreasonable or exorbitant?

sections.label: Revisions to copyright duration
sections.summary: Clauses 114, 122 and 125 introduced a number of revisions to copyright duration.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clauses 114, 122 and 125 introduced a number of revisions to copyright duration.

sections.label: Copyright term extension to 70 years
sections.summary: Limiting copyright protection to 70 years after the creator's passing rather than the date of publication extends the protection period.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Similarly, it is worth observing that the decision to limit copyright protection to 70 years following the creator's passing as opposed to the date of publication, as was the case previously, amounts to an extension of the period of protection.

sections.label: Clause 121(b) and EU-Singapore FTA
sections.summary: Clause 121(b) provides for copyright and sound recordings and was included to respect Singapore's obligations under the EU-Singapore FTA.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 121(b) of the Bill provides for copyright and sound recordings and was included to respect Singapore's obligations under the EU-Singapore FTA.

sections.label: Clause 135 automatic ownership commission works
sections.summary: Clause 135 grants certain authors automatic ownership of copyright over commission works, strengthening creators' legal standing over their intellectual property.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On one hand, clause 135 grants certain authors automatic ownership of copyright over commission works thereby strengthening legal standing of creators over their intellectual property.

sections.label: Default rights vest in creator
sections.summary: The speaker prefers defaulting rights to the creator, with any transfer to the employer and associated compensation explicitly drafted into the employment contract.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In my view, it is better for the default to vest the rights to the creator and have any rights transfer to the employer along with associated compensation be explicitly drafted into the employment contract.

sections.label: Reasonable portion copying percentages
sections.summary: Clause 194(1b) allows copying a reasonable portion, which clause 197(2c) specifies as 5% or five pages for literary or dramatic works.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 194(1b) allows for a reasonable portion of the work to be copied which clause 197(2c), for instance, specifies as 5% or five pages, depending on the total length of a literary or dramatic work.

sections.label: Academic publishers and public access
sections.summary: Academic publishers have been accused of exploiting free academic labour and expensive library subscriptions, prompting open access deals and an EU public funding mandate.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Members in this House may be aware that a number of international academic publishing houses have been accused of exploiting free labour from civic-minded academics and subsequently turning around and burdening libraries with expensive subscriptions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It took the University of California, the largest public university system in the world, two whole years of bruising contract negotiations to finally arrive at a deal that would allow its faculty and students open access to Elsevier journals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The European Union, in an effort to prevent paying double for publicly-funded knowledge – once to fund the research, another to access it behind a copyrighted paywall – has even gone as far as to mandate that the output of any project that benefits from public funding must remain freely accessible.

sections.label: Workers' Party supports intellectual property
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports recognition of intellectual property in works of authors and performers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party supports the recognition of intellectual property in the works of authors and performers.

sections.label: Courts deferral on fair use
sections.summary: Deferring to the Courts on a case-by-case basis what constitutes fair use may be a sound way forward, and this Bill does this.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To this end, a deferral to the Courts, on a case-by-case basis, of what constitutes fair use may well represent a sound way forward; and this Bill does this.

sections.label: Ministry technical capability fair use
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry will ensure technical capability to evaluate the merits of fair use provisions is available in such cases.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To this end, how will the Ministry ensure that the technical capability to evaluate the merits of fair use provisions is available in cases of this nature?

sections.label: Legislators balancing the two
sections.summary: The onus is on legislators and policymakers to try to get the balance between the two right.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The onus is on us then, as legislators and policymakers, to try to get the balance between the two right.

sections.label: Rights of creators and performers
sections.summary: It proposes granting creators and performers attribution rights and default ownership of certain commissioned works.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: First, granting creators and performers the right to be attributed and identified whenever their works or performances are used in public; and second, granting creators default ownership of certain types of commissioned works.

sections.label: Default ownership and bargaining position
sections.summary: Granting creators default ownership of certain commissioned works would improve their bargaining position before negotiations begin.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In addition, by granting creators default ownership of certain types of commissioned works, they would be in a better bargaining position before negotiations begin.

sections.label: Freelancers' concerns with Government contracts
sections.summary: Freelancers say Government contracts contain onerous clauses on unlimited revisions, payment on completion, and full IP assignment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Feedback from freelancers I met are that Government contracts contain overly onerous clauses, for which the Government is reluctant to compromise on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I will share some of the clauses which freelancers are uncomfortable with, namely, the Government’s right to require freelancers to make an unlimited number of revisions or changes to the product(s); payment by the Government only upon completion and delivery of products and/or services; and complete assignment of all IP rights associated with the products to the Government.

sections.label: Payment timing and IP reuse
sections.summary: Payment only on completion means tight finances, and assigned IP rights let the Government keep reusing materials without re-engaging freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Second, payment only upon completion and delivery of the products would mean living within tight financial constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Third, I am told that once the IP rights of the materials or contents have been wholly assigned to the Government, upon expiry of the contract, the Government continues to re-use and replicate the same set of materials multiple times over the years, without engaging freelancers for their subsequent services over the years.

sections.label: Reuse of content after single payment
sections.summary: Service buyers reuse and republish creators' content or performances on multiple occasions despite paying only for a single performance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Service buyers re-use and/or republish the content/performance of creators on various digital platforms on multiple occasions, despite only paying for a single performance.

sections.label: Digital events and freelancer pay
sections.summary: Digital events let buyers screen performances on multiple platforms, so freelancers are paid once instead of multiple times as before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: However, in today's context where most events are held digitally, service buyers have also resorted to publishing and/or screening these performances and recordings on multiple platforms, on various occasions to different audiences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This would mean that freelancers are only paid once for their recorded performances when they would have been paid multiple times for their performances in a pre-pandemic era.

sections.label: Flexibility for freelancers in COVID-19
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to show flexibility and compassion towards freelancers during COVID-19 while acknowledging the need for watertight contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: While we understand that watertight contracts are needed to safeguard the Government's rights, we would humbly ask that the Government exercise flexibility and compassion towards the freelancers, especially in this COVID-19 season.

sections.label: LawWorks legal primer on copyright
sections.summary: NTUC, IPOS and Law Society Pro Bono Services will hold a LawWorks legal primer in October on the copyright amendments to educate freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: On NTUC's Labour Movement's end, together with IPOS and Law Society Pro Bono Services (BPSO), we will be conducting a LawWorks legal primer covering this set of copyright amendments in October to educate freelancers on it and address any questions that they may have.

sections.label: Events and performing arts standstill
sections.summary: Circuit breaker measures and restrictions on social gatherings have brought the events and performing arts sector, including getai, almost to a standstill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: With the circuit breaker measures that were implemented last year, together with the existing restrictions on social gatherings, the events and performing arts sector, including getai, has almost come to a standstill.

sections.label: More needed for freelancers
sections.summary: The speaker submits that while the Copyright Act amendments will improve freelancers' lives, more can and should be done for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: While the amendments to the Copyright Act will improve the lives of freelancers, it is humbly submitted that more can and should be done for them.

sections.label: Right to be identified
sections.summary: Divisions 1 and 2 of Part 7 automatically grant authors and performers the right to be identified, going further than the current false attribution regime.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Divisions 1 and 2 of Part 7 automatically grant authors the right to be identified in relation to the works they produce and performers to be identified with their performances.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is a welcome step further than the current regime under which creators and performers only have a right to prevent the false attribution of another person as the author or performer.

sections.label: Workers' Party support for more rights
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports going further than the Bill to give creators and performers more rights, protections and rewards in line with developed countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The system in Singapore surrounding creative practitioners is therefore still very much tied with the involvement and endorsement of the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Therefore, the Workers' Party would support a move that goes even further than the current Bill in giving more rights, protections and rewards to creators and performers to be in line with those in developed countries.

sections.label: Fair use clarification for online content
sections.summary: Asks whether the Minister will clarify what constitutes fair use for online content or await court guidance in litigation.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given that an increasing number of Singaporeans are creating online content, will the Minister provide any further clarification on what would constitute "fair use" or would this await the guidance of the Courts when the matter has been taken to litigation?

sections.label: Text and data mining exception
sections.summary: Part 5 Division 8 permits reproduction of works and performances for computational data analysis, commercially and non-commercially, with conditions including lawful access.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moving on to a new exception contained in Part 5, Division 8 which is for the reproduction of works for text and data mining.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This applies to both commercial and non-commercial activities and would permit reproduction of works and recordings of performances for "computational data analysis", including the preparation of works for analysis.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: There are protective conditions in clause 244(2), which amongst others, specify that the user must have had lawful access to the work or recording.

sections.label: Euro 2020 paywall fee
sections.summary: The Euro 2020 football tournament was available only to those paying over $90 for all matches.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The recent Euro 2020 football tournament was available only to those who could pay the exorbitant fee of over $90 to have access to all matches.

sections.label: Sports Plus subscription cost
sections.summary: Watching Roger Federer requires paying about $49.90 monthly or $449 yearly for Sports Plus, plus navigating confusing channels and exclusivity changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Nowadays, if I want to see if Roger Federer would ever win another Slam, I would need to pay around $49.90 a month or $449 a year for the Sports Plus package to watch it on TV after spending lots of time and effort navigating the confusing variety of different sports, the different channels and providers offer and deal with changes to availability due to exclusivity rights expiring.

sections.label: Paid TV divide and sports access
sections.summary: Paid TV after the Singtel-StarHub duopoly divided those who can afford top sports from those who cannot, prompting questions on widening access as set-top box liability is imposed.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Television used to be a great equaliser in Singapore, but it is ironic and saddening that the advent of paid TV in the wake of the duopoly between Singtel and StarHub – which was ostensibly to give the audience greater choice – has now opened up a divide between those who can afford to pay more to watch top sports competitions and those who cannot afford to do so.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Now that the Government is going to impose civil and criminal liability for commercial dealings in set-top boxes and related services, what steps will the Government take to widen access to broadcast of sporting events?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Will certain popular sporting events be broadcast free-to-air or perhaps be shown at Community Clubs?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Speaker, television used to be a great equaliser in Singapore but it is ironic that the advent of paid TV in the wake of the duopoly between Singtel and StarHub, which was, ostensibly, to give us greater choice, has now opened up a divide between those who can afford to pay the extra subscription charges to watch top sports competitions and those who cannot afford to do so.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Now that civil and criminal liability for commercial dealings in set-top boxes and related services is being imposed, what steps will the Government take to widen access to broadcast of sporting events?

sections.label: Copies for computational data analysis
sections.summary: The Bill explicitly permits making copies and using copyright works for computational data analysis, subject to conditions and safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, the Bill makes it explicit that it is permitted to make copies and use copyright works for the purposes of computational data analysis, subject to certain conditions and safeguards.

sections.label: Non-profit schools digital resources copyright
sections.summary: The Bill lets non-profit schools and students use freely available digital resources for education with citation, and allows print-disabled format conversions without licence fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill also now makes clear that non-profit schools and their students may use digital resources that are freely available for educational uses without having to seek permission from each copyright owner as long as they are cited with the date of access of the said material.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This update is important to keep our copyright regime current and relevant in light of the changing sources and mediums of works.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am also particularly heartened by clause 214 of the Bill, which will allow for conversions of works into formats accessible by print-disabled users without having to pay licence fees to the copyright owner.

sections.label: Creators default copyright owners
sections.summary: The Copyright Bill standardises that creators of works are the default owners of the copyrights to those works.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, the Copyright Bill will now standardise the position that the creators of works will be the default owners of the copyrights to these works.

sections.label: Marrakesh Treaty print-disabled remuneration
sections.summary: The 2015 exceptions implemented Singapore's Marrakesh Treaty commitments, and the obligation to pay equitable remuneration for print-disabled conversions is removed, though it remains for Persons with Intellectual Disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These exceptions were introduced in 2015 to implement Singapore's commitments under the World Intellectual Property Organization's (WIPO) Marrakesh Treaty.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am further heartened to know that the obligation for authorised entities to pay equitable remuneration for converting copyrighted works is removed, thus making access for the print-disabled easier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, I would like to clarify why this obligation remains for Persons with Intellectual Disabilities, as stated in Division 5 of section 217(3).

sections.label: Removing remuneration for intellectual disabilities
sections.summary: The speaker proposes removing the obligation for authorised entities to pay equitable remuneration to copyright owners for copies made for Persons with Intellectual Disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As such, I would like to propose to remove the obligation for authorised entities to pay equitable remuneration to copyright owners for making, distributing or making available copies of copyrighted works for Persons with Intellectual Disabilities.

sections.label: Extending provisions to hearing disability
sections.summary: Noting limits in auto-transcription quality and the need for manual transcription, the speaker asks whether print-disabled provisions can be extended to persons with hearing disability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although technology and artificial intelligence tools may be able to enable auto-transcription, but there are also limitations in the quality of transcriptions and hence, the need for manual transcription, which requires access to copyrighted materials.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask whether the current provisions for print-disabled persons can also be extended to persons with hearing disability.

sections.label: Culture attributing creators
sections.summary: The speaker's first point is on creating a culture that attributes creators, shown in the amendment allowing schools and students to use freely available Internet resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: My first point is on creating a culture that attributes creators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is shown in the amendment which allows schools and students to use freely available resources from the Internet.

sections.label: Mediation fees per party
sections.summary: The cheapest option appears to be a $50 administrative fee and a $500 mediator fee per party for a four-hour session.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The cheapest option appears to be an administrative fee of $50 per party and a mediator fee of $500 per party for a four-hour session.

sections.label: Copyright infringement mediation costs overseas
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a guilty party should bear all mediation costs and whether the laws affect overseas infringers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, if any copyright infringement has been found, the guilty party should be made to bear the entire mediation costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: My other concern is whether these laws would have any impact, if the copyright infringement is committed by individuals or organisations overseas.

sections.label: Combining copied materials into publications
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether copied materials can be incorporated into an existing publication with other content without seeking permission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While the Bill states that the materials can be copied, I wish to clarify whether such materials can be incorporated into an existing publication, like a pamphlet that also contains other content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In essence, can contents from different sources be combined, without the need to seek permission?

sections.label: Clarification on home businesses and freelancing
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister for clarification, noting pandemic job losses led more Singaporeans to set up home businesses or freelance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide some clarification on this?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Job losses as a result of the pandemic saw many more Singaporeans setting up their home businesses or freelancing.

sections.label: Designers undercut using pitch references
sections.summary: The speaker describes clients contracting cheaper designers who use another designer's pitch as a reference without wholesale plagiarism.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Many think that the process goes like this: the designer offers a great idea, the client likes it, they contract with the designer and the designer goes on to make their design a success for the client.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, how transactions often go is like this: the designer still offers great design ideas, the client still falls in love with that idea, but they contract with another designer who might be willing to take a smaller cut and this designer who is willing to do it for less is given the pitch from the other designer as a "reference", effectively clearing themselves of all hoops presented by our laws as they stand, as long as the "reference" is not plagiarised wholesale.

sections.label: Resident's likeness commercialised without recourse
sections.summary: The speaker describes a resident whose likeness an artist illustrated and commercialised, with no recognised image or personality rights in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: You could imagine my resident's dismay, however, when it was revealed that an artist had illustrated her likeness from one of her test-shoot photos and went on to commercialise and profit off her piece of work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This, certainly, was not Miss Duan's first experience with her likeness being appropriated by others.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: But without the firm recognition of image or personality rights in Singapore, she was fully subject to the cooperation and compliance of the other party.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, for my resident, on this occasion, the other party was unwilling to make recourse.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is necessary that we have the regulatory environment shaped in such a way that our Creatives' "rice bowls" do not rest shakily on the goodwill of strangers.

sections.label: Copying for computational data analysis
sections.summary: Section 244 permits copying works for computational data analysis, and section 187 bars creators from restricting this by contract.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 244 permits the copying of the works for the purposes of computational data analysis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under section 187, creators are not allowed to restrict this by contract.

sections.label: Moral right of identification
sections.summary: Part 7 of the Bill gives a work's author a moral right to be identified if another person causes the work to be published.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Part 7 of the Bill provides a moral right for the author of a work to be identified if another person causes that work to be published.

sections.label: Attribution and default copyright ownership
sections.summary: The new Copyright Act gives creators and performers attribution rights and grants default copyright ownership for commissioned photographs, portraits and engravings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the new Copyright Act, creators and performers have the right to be attributed when their work or performance is used.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Also, creators of certain works including commissioned photographs, portraits and engravings will be granted default copyright ownership.

sections.label: Legal recourse for freelance creators
sections.summary: The question asks how freelance creators with little resources can seek legal recourse without delay to protect their reputation and commercial value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In the digital era where such content may be rapidly replicated and distributed, can the Minister share how freelance creators with little resources can seek legal recourse without delay to better protect their reputation and commercial value of their work?

sections.label: CMOs, attribution and foreign infringers
sections.summary: The passage asks about protecting contributors to computational data analysis, CMO relationships with local and overseas owners, a valuation framework, and suing foreign infringers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: There is a more critical need for Singapore as we need to continue to be relevant as a global business hub and evolve together with emerging trends and challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, there are scenarios where the work of a creator or collective is pivotal to the outcome of the computational data analysis, for example, if 90% of the data was from an individual or a collective, without their significant contribution, this study would not have been possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Does the Ministry have measures to protect the rights of these individuals, given their significant contribution, to ensure that there is proper attribution and protection of their reputation and commercial interest?

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: On CMOs, the aim is "to build a fair, safe and transparent system where CMOs, rights owners and future generations can reap the rewards of an efficient copyright ecosystem".

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, due to the transnational nature of the copyright ecosystem, can the Minister share how these new measures affect the relationship between CMOs and copyright owners based in Singapore and overseas, especially when the relationship is between a foreign-based distributor and local freelance creator?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will MinLaw work with MAS and the accountancy sector to develop a valuation and financing framework so that the copyright can be valued, collateralised and be encashed?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Are there any other avenue which can allow a Singaporean copyright holder to sue a foreign infringer?

sections.label: Print-disabled format conversion remuneration
sections.summary: Under the Copyright Bill, such persons will no longer pay remuneration where a print copy must be converted into other formats for the print-disabled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under the Copyright Bill, such persons will no longer be required to pay remuneration in situations where a print copy needs to be converted into other formats to benefit those who are print-disabled.

sections.label: Paying for sports broadcasts
sections.summary: A member urges MinLaw to discuss with MCCY whether the Government can pay for broadcasts of popular sports events.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Popular sports events such as the English Premier League, the World Cup and NBA can only be watched through paying expensive subscription fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I would like urge MinLaw to discuss with MCCY and explore whether the Government can pay for the broadcast?

sections.label: Balancing copyright framework interests
sections.summary: The Bill balances competing interests so that public access to content and recognition and attribution for creators are both allowed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Conversely, too tight a framework on copyright with less exceptions, tighter fair use, might mean that public interests and access might then not be fulfilled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, in designing this Bill, we have had to tread a balanced path, look at all the competing interests and balance it one against the other and find a path that at once, allows public interests in content but at the same time, creates an environment where creators can be recognised and attributed for their works.

sections.label: Creators forming industry associations
sections.summary: Creators should consider coming together to form industry associations that develop industry best practices to represent them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Creators should instead consider coming together, forming industry associations to develop industry best practices to represent them.

sections.label: Specialised IP litigation track
sections.summary: A simplified, cost-saving specialised IP litigation track in the High Court is about to be introduced, with details announced in coming months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Members might recall that in 2019, I mentioned during the Second Reading of the Intellectual Property (Dispute Resolution) Bill that MinLaw and the Supreme Court were looking into the introduction of a specialised IP litigation "track" in the High Court with simplified processes and cost-saving features.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That simplified process track is about to be introduced and more details will be announced in the coming months.

sections.label: Territorial copyright enforcement
sections.summary: Copyright laws are territorial, and Singapore's regime lets rights owners enforce against infringements occurring in Singapore by locals or foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: A fundamental point is that copyright laws are territorial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Our copyright regime allows rights owners to enforce against acts of infringement that occur in Singapore, regardless of whether they are by a local or a foreigner.

sections.label: Contracts before Bill's effective date
sections.summary: Clause 135 clarifies that contracts entered into before the Bill's effective date will not be affected by the changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Clause 135 of the Bill clarifies that contracts entered into prior to the effective date of this Bill will not be affected by the changes I spoke about.

sections.label: Liability for commercial dealers
sections.summary: The new provisions impose liability on those who deal commercially with such boxes, like sellers, but not buyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The new provisions impose liability on those who deal commercially with such boxes, like sellers, but not the buyers of such boxes.

sections.label: Computational analysis and contract terms
sections.summary: Computational data analysis does not use the expressive nature of works, and many permitted uses can be modified or excluded by reasonable contract terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Computational data analysis treats the works as data points and does not make use of the expressive nature of the works, which is what copyright fundamentally seeks to protect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To Mr Louis Ng's question, many permitted uses can be modified or excluded via reasonable contract terms.

sections.label: Contractual restrictions on data analysis
sections.summary: Locking specific databases out of the analysis through contractual restrictions would make results less useful or create bias or inaccuracies, so private contracts should not override this permitted use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Having specific databases locked out of the analysis because of contractual restrictions would make the results less useful, or worse, create bias or inaccuracies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Therefore, it is important not to allow private contractual provisions to override this permitted use.

sections.label: Dropping the fifth factor
sections.summary: Despite dropping the fifth factor, Courts can still consider it when relevant; it was dropped because stakeholders said it caused confusion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I would also add that despite dropping the fifth factor, the Courts can still consider that factor when relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We dropped the fifth factor because there was market feedback by stakeholders that it lent itself into confusion.

sections.label: CMO prices not controlled
sections.summary: The regulations proposed in this Bill do not control the prices which CMOs charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As I mentioned briefly earlier, our regulations proposed in this Bill do not control the prices which CMOs charge.

sections.label: Clause 459 and CMO regulations
sections.summary: Clause 459 clarifies the new regulations apply to any CMO offering licences in Singapore, but not foreign CMOs offering licences overseas, and will be implemented later after public consultation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Clause 459 of the Bill clarifies that the new regulations will apply to any CMO who offers licences to users in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: However, foreign CMOs who represent local rights owners, but offer licences to users overseas, will not be subject to the new regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The provisions for regulating the CMOs will only be implemented later after a further public consultation on licence conditions next year.

sections.label: IPOS website materials on changes
sections.summary: IPOS has posted materials on its website explaining the changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: IPOS has put up materials on their website, explaining the changes.

sections.label: Geographical Indications Act local producers
sections.summary: The previous Geographical Indications Act does not stop local producers producing, but they cannot use a name referencing a location.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That had been covered in the previous Geographical Indications Act, which we had passed earlier and amended last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But I would like to assure the House that it does not stop local producers from producing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: You just cannot call it a name that otherwise bears a reference to a location.

sections.label: Members support Bill rights balance
sections.summary: Members who spoke support the Bill, which represents commitment to balance between rights owners and users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I think all of the Members who have spoken support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This Bill represents our commitment to ensure that balance between rights owners and the users.
